gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the warranties it ranks on mean different things: EG4's '10-year' LifePower4 V2 warranty is 'prorated 1/10th per year after the first year', and Epoch's '11-year' warranty on the V2-T Elite replaces the battery free only in years 1–5 and then offers 40% off MSRP. Their cycle ratings also use different end points: EG4 states '>6,000 cycles at 80% DoD' with no end-of-life capacity, and Epoch states '3,500+ cycles (to 70% capacity)'.
standout_why: I compared against the cited liveoffthegrid.com/specs/batteries table, its EG4 LifePower4 V2 detail page, and ownyourelectricity.com/articles/48-volt-lithium-battery. liveoffthegrid gives one 'Warranty' number per battery (EG4 '10 yr', Pytes '10 yr') and cycles only as '@ DoD'. It names no end-of-life capacity for any battery and says nothing about prorating. Its EG4 V2 page took its figures from the V1.0 sheet. ownyourelectricity gives no warranty terms and no end-of-life percentages. ChatGPT's own answer lists '10 years preferred, with clear replacement terms' as a criterion but describes EG4 only as having 'a 10-year warranty' and doesn't say what Epoch's covers. One gap in my check: the cited EG4 V2 spec sheet PDF came back as compressed binary, so I couldn't confirm that it doesn't carry the proration note. Because it's a spec sheet and not a warranty document, that's unlikely.
decides: The finding doesn't change who wins, but it changes why. EG4 still wins on price per kWh and cycle claims, but its '10-year warranty' is full only in year 1 and prorated after that, so the page shouldn't present it as 10 years of full replacement. Epoch's premium price ($2,599 at Epoch today, up from the $2,399 ChatGPT showed) buys 5 years of free repair or replacement, not 11. Its cycle claim (3,500 to 70%) is also stated against a lower end point than the others, so the page shouldn't read it as close to EG4's 6,000. For golf carts, LiTime's '200A' battery holds 200 A for 2 minutes. Its cheaper Bluetooth 48V 100Ah sibling is rated 1C (100 A) continuous with a 600 A one-second peak.

findings.value: 10 years, prorated 1/10th per year after the first year
findings.source_title: Warranty - EG4 LifePower4 48V v2 Battery - EG4 Electronics
findings.note: Exact wording: '10-year Full Parts Replacement or Full Product Replacement Prorated Warranty', 'prorated 1/10th per year after the first year'. You must register within the first year or keep proof of purchase from an authorized distributor. Reselling the battery or removing it from its original installation site voids the warranty. No capacity-retention threshold or throughput cap is stated.
